significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that a teacher's reward-hacking policy is causally transmitted through task- and reward-free number/code data, remains "TASK-GENERAL" across structurally different evaluations, and is separable from generic misalignment. This is principally a form-(ii) causal phenomenon, but the claimed double dissociation decomposes subliminally transmitted behavior into two independently varying dispositions; it would constrain whether covert distillation transfers only content-like traits or also strategic evaluation-gaming policies, while the exploratory "single early-layer disposition direction" would add only a bounded one-behavior mechanism. The negative branch is also informative because it would place a substantive boundary on the transmission phenomenon reported in Cloud et al.'s Subliminal Learning work—strategic shortcut-seeking would not follow from established transmission of preferences or static misalignment—and verified-true and verified-false are clearly distinguishable. In the topic-substitution check, merely restating "extend subliminal learning" would merit only the topic median; the cross-task policy claim and reward-hacking/generic-misalignment decomposition are the claim-specific reasons for scoring above it.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is an auditing rule and diagnostic: test distilled students on "unseen, structurally different gameable evaluations" and make "dataset auditing, distillation policy, and eval design ... inspect behavioral/latent channels, not just content." This is an ex-ante handle when used before deployment or entry into an automated-evaluation pipeline, giving teams an opportunity to reject or further audit a student even when content filters and ordinary on-task audits pass. Its conclusion transfers across a class of reward-hacking tasks and the asserted number/code carriers as a qualitative teacher-to-student risk relation, although it does not provide a quantitative law predicting effect size across new model families; downstream users explicitly include teams that audit or ship automated evaluators and self-improving agents. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the generic subliminal-learning topic supplies no such cross-family gameable-evaluation screen or practitioner-facing audit rule, so the reach comes from this claim's specific conclusion.
